chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from al-Qasim bin Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, from al-Fadl bin 'Ayyadh, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Do you know who the avaricious one is? I said: Is he the stingy one? He said: The avaricious one is worse than the stingy one. Indeed, the stingy one is stingy with what is in his hands, and the avaricious one is avaricious with what is in the hands of people as well as what is in his own hands, until he does not see anything in the hands of people except that he wishes for it to be his, whether through the lawful or the forbidden. He does not become satisfied, nor is he content, with what Allah, Exalted is He, has sustained him.

key_terms.الشَّحِيحُ: The avaricious one; one who is intensely greedy for wealth and possessions
key_terms.الْبَخِيلُ: The stingy one; one who hoards what he possesses and refuses to give
key_terms.بِالْحَلِّ وَالْحَرَامِ: Through the lawful and the forbidden; regardless of legality
key_terms.يَشْحُ: He is avaricious/greedy; to desire intensely
key_terms.يَقْنَعُ: He is content/satisfied; to be pleased with what one has

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between stinginess (bukhl) and avarice (shah) in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s nuanced distinction between the stingy (*al-bakhil*), who hoards his own wealth, and the avaricious (*al-shahih*), whose greed is all-consuming. The avaricious individual is described as insatiable, desiring both his own possessions and those of others, regardless of whether they are acquired through lawful (*halal*) or unlawful (*haram*) means. This highlights a spiritual deficiency where one lacks *qana'ah* (contentment) with Allah’s decree, leading to a perpetual state of dissatisfaction with divine sustenance.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Qasem bin Muhammed al-Esbahani, from Sulayman bin Dawud al-Manqari, from Fudail bin ‘Ayyadh, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

Do you know who the avaricious is? I said: Is he the stingy? He said: The avaricious is worse than the stingy. Indeed, a stingy person is stingy with what is in his own hand, and the avaricious person is avaricious with what is in the hands of people as well as what is in his own hand, until he does not see in the hands of people anything except that he wishes for it to be his, (regardless if it is earned) through (the) lawful and the forbidden. He does not become satisfied, nor is he content, with what Allah, Exalted is He, has sustained him.
